title: Interpretable Feature Discovery from Unstructured Data Using LLMs and Statistical Choice Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.38082v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Feature extraction from unstructured data typically relies on opaque embeddings unsuited to interpretable decision-making. Interpretable features, on the other hand, typically require costly, and often infeasible, hand-engineering. Large language models (LLMs) offer a natural bridge, as they can read raw data and describe it in interpretable terms. One could simply ask an LLM to extract features from a large sample of the dataset, but context limitations and diluted attention can lead to unsatisfactory results. We introduce a method that automatically discovers interpretable, decision-relevant features from unstructured data. Our key idea is to perform pairwise comparisons between items, asking an LLM to articulate, in interpretable terms, the features distinguishing each pair. translated_title: 利用大语言模型与统计选择模型从非结构化数据中发现可解释特征
translated_abstract: 从非结构化数据中进行特征提取通常依赖于不透明的嵌入表示，难以支持可解释的决策；而可解释特征则通常需要成本高昂、甚至常常不可行的手工设计。大语言模型（LLM）为此提供了一座天然的桥梁，因为它们能够读取原始数据并以可解释的术语对其进行描述。然而，直接让LLM从数据集的大量样本中提取特征，可能会因上下文长度限制和注意力稀释而导致结果不尽如人意。我们提出了一种从非结构化数据中自动发现可解释且与决策相关特征的方法。其核心思想是对物品进行成对比较，让LLM用可解释的术语阐明区分每一对物品的特征。我们将这些解释（即理由/rationales）视为数据：我们开发了一个统计选择模型，将这些理由在多次比较中进行汇总，从而识别出相关的特征。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种新方法，通过让大语言模型对物品进行成对比较并生成可解释的理由，再用统计选择模型聚合这些理由，从而自动从非结构化数据中发现可解释且与决策相关的特征。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a method that automatically discovers interpretable, decision-relevant features from unstructured data by having LLMs articulate pairwise-distinguishing rationales and aggregating them with a statistical choice model.
